data.content_ref: inline:The target mislabels a deterministic writer as 'idempotent.' It claims 'a writer that appends a deterministic hash of the payload is both safe and idempotent (same payload always yields the same entry, deduplicatable).' But idempotency in the f(f(x))=f(x) sense means retrying the write produces the same log state as a single write—i.e., the log contains one entry, not duplicate identical entries. A deterministic-hash writer still appends a new (content-identical) entry on every retry, growing the log. The parenthetical 'deduplicatable' reveals that collapse to a single entry is a processor-side operation, not a writer property. Thus the target conflates determinism (same input → same output) with idempotency (applying twice = applying once), undermining the very distinction between 'safe' and 'idempotent' that the problem asks it to clarify.
